body.x: Seoreu (CEO Yeoun Joo Lee) announced its participation in CES 2025, which will be held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7th (Tuesday) to January 10th (Friday). The company will showcase its AI-powered capsule endoscopy video analysis system, CAPTOS, at the "K-Startup Pavilion."

Seoreu has been dedicated to developing proprietary AI technologies that aim to revolutionize the treatment and management of gastrointestinal diseases. The company aims to provide reliable data for diagnostics, prognosis management, and regular health checkups, enabling individuals to easily access high-quality medical services.

Previously, Seoreu gained industry recognition with its capsule endoscopy reading assistance program, which addressed a critical demand in medical practices. The company has since expanded its portfolio to cover a broader range of gastrointestinal technologies and products. It has also secured large-scale projects for building medical datasets, focusing on acquiring medical imaging essential for AI development while addressing the high costs of large-scale data processing.

At CES 2025, Seoreu will introduce its CAPTOS system. This system analyzes capsule endoscopy videos using AI to identify and accurately analyze various small bowel lesions. It employs quantitative analysis to distinguish disease severity, facilitating prompt and precise diagnoses. This technology is particularly effective for the early diagnosis and treatment planning of pediatric Crohn's disease (CD).

The CAPTOS system’s AI algorithm features three main capabilities: identifying the small intestine by accurately distinguishing the position of the stomach, small intestine, and large intestine; detecting and distinguishing four key types of lesions essential for disease diagnosis; and determining the visible range within the small intestine. These algorithms also summarize critical lesions and generate automated reports, including accuracy assessments.

This functionality significantly reduces the time medical professionals spend reviewing and analyzing data. It eliminates concerns about diagnostic errors caused by human mistakes, offering patients highly reliable results. CAPTOS has demonstrated diagnostic accuracy of up to 95% compared to experienced medical professionals.

A Seoreu representative stated, “CAPTOS AI supports the assessment of lesion severity through quantitative analysis. It is optimized not only for pediatric CD but also for adult CD diagnostics. The algorithm, trained and refined using intestinal image data from over 500 pediatric CD patients, achieves exceptional accuracy. It is also compatible with various hardware systems, allowing comparison of results from different capsule endoscopy devices.”

The representative continued, “By revolutionizing the diagnostic and treatment processes for Crohn's disease, CAPTOS AI has immense utility beyond Korea, particularly in countries that share modernized dietary habits and meat-centric diets. At CES 2025, we aim to establish a foothold in markets such as Central Asia, including Kazakhstan, where Crohn’s disease cases are rapidly increasing, as well as in the U.S. and Europe.”
